findings.desc: overflow_auto bypasses its documented visible-approval guard: core/lattice-dispatch starts the dispatch when either approve=true or start=true is present, so --start=true alone materializes dispatch state even though the CLI/docs promise suggest-only behavior unless visibly approved. This breaks the manual-first user-visible contract for overflow_auto.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 74ce419c. overflow_auto now requires approve=true and start=true; fake dispatch paths are bounded before any file write; scaffolded real-host dispatch creates the projected worktree or returns failed with warnings. Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build, npm --prefix packages/main run test:dispatch-run-smoke, npm --prefix packages/main run test:lattice-handoff-smoke, npm run test:command-ownership-contract, and npm run test:process-fact-contract.

findings.desc: [HIGH] packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:845 and 1054-1066 leave approved real-host dispatch_run/overflow_auto without a usable overflow worktree. prepareDispatch writes only metadata and explicitly leaves worktree creation undone, but the scaffolded real-host run path tells the operator to run codex/claude/gemini in .worktrees/overflow/... anyway. Repro: node packages/main/dist/cli.js --root <tmp> lattice dispatch run --storyId=B-real --host=codex --json returned status=needs_receipt with nextAction pointing at .worktrees/overflow/B-real/D-B-real-codex-..., while the recorded dispatch.json showed worktreeExists=false for that path. That breaks the required host-overflow workflow in docs/requirements/decisions/host-overflow.md:52-54, where Lattice must project an isolated overflow worktree before the host works in it, so the approved real-host overflow path cannot actually execute.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 74ce419c. overflow_auto now requires approve=true and start=true; fake dispatch paths are bounded before any file write; scaffolded real-host dispatch creates the projected worktree or returns failed with warnings. Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build, npm --prefix packages/main run test:dispatch-run-smoke, npm --prefix packages/main run test:lattice-handoff-smoke, npm run test:command-ownership-contract, and npm run test:process-fact-contract.

findings.desc: Verified HIGH: overflow_auto starts a mutating dispatch when either --start=true or --approve=true is present because the guard is `if (args.start !== true && args.approve !== true) return plan`. That contradicts the CLI contract (`requires visible approval to start`) and CHK-008 requireApproval semantics. Repro: a throwaway registry run returned lattice.dispatch_run.v1 accepted_local for both startOnly={start:true} and approveOnly={approve:true}. The command currently bypasses its explicit approval/start safety policy.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 74ce419c. overflow_auto now requires approve=true and start=true; fake dispatch paths are bounded before any file write; scaffolded real-host dispatch creates the projected worktree or returns failed with warnings. Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build, npm --prefix packages/main run test:dispatch-run-smoke, npm --prefix packages/main run test:lattice-handoff-smoke, npm run test:command-ownership-contract, and npm run test:process-fact-contract.

findings.desc: Verified HIGH: fake dispatch_run writes pack.allowedPaths[0] directly via path.join(worktreeAbs, markerPath) before any scope validation, so ../../ traversal escapes the isolated overflow worktree. Repro: a throwaway registry run with allowedPaths=["../../escape.txt"] created .worktrees/overflow/escape.txt and only failed later at git add. This breaks the bounded-path contract for dispatch_run/overflow_auto and allows out-of-scope filesystem writes.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 74ce419c. overflow_auto now requires approve=true and start=true; fake dispatch paths are bounded before any file write; scaffolded real-host dispatch creates the projected worktree or returns failed with warnings. Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build, npm --prefix packages/main run test:dispatch-run-smoke, npm --prefix packages/main run test:lattice-handoff-smoke, npm run test:command-ownership-contract, and npm run test:process-fact-contract.

findings.desc: Verified HIGH: 74ce419c still allows fake dispatch_run to write outside the isolated overflow worktree via tracked symlink paths. The new assertWorktreeRelativePath()/normalizeFakePackPaths guard in packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts only rejects absolute and .. segments, but runFakeLeafDispatch then resolves markerAbs and writes it directly before any canonical-path check. Repro: after npm --prefix packages/main run build, a one-off registry run in a temporary git repo with a tracked absolute symlink packages/main/src/generated/escape-link -> /tmp/... prepared dispatchId=D-symlink with allowedPaths=["packages/main/src/generated/escape-link/escaped.txt"]. dispatch_run threw later at git add with fatal: pathspec ... is beyond a symbolic link, but /tmp/.../escaped.txt had already been created with dispatch metadata. This means the bounded fake-path write contract is still bypassable before the command fails.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 990be1be. Fake dispatch now uses canonical realpath containment before mkdir/write so symlink escapes fail before external writes. README and host-overflow docs now describe landed dispatch_plan/prepare/run/overflow_auto, approve+start gating, and real-host worktree creation/failure behavior. Verified with build, dispatch-run smoke, lattice-handoff smoke, command ownership contract, and process fact contract.

findings.desc: README.md:76, README.md:99, docs/requirements/decisions/host-overflow.md:35 MEDIUM: docs still present dispatch_plan/dispatch_prepare/dispatch_run as future work and only show the older handoff/host_dispatch flow, but the local CLI/code already ship overflow_auto with a visible approve+start gate and dispatch_run that creates a real-host worktree before needs_receipt or returns failed on scaffold errors. Update the docs to describe the landed dispatch surfaces and these approval/worktree semantics.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 990be1be. Fake dispatch now uses canonical realpath containment before mkdir/write so symlink escapes fail before external writes. README and host-overflow docs now describe landed dispatch_plan/prepare/run/overflow_auto, approve+start gating, and real-host worktree creation/failure behavior. Verified with build, dispatch-run smoke, lattice-handoff smoke, command ownership contract, and process fact contract.

findings.desc: Real-host dispatch_run can scaffold an isolated overflow worktree while preserving allowedPaths/deniedPaths that point outside that worktree, so the generated prompt can instruct a real host to edit ../outside.txt. Fake dispatch paths are bounded, but real-host scaffold does not validate pack paths before writing prompt/worktree metadata or returning needs_receipt. Repro: prepare a codex dispatch with allowedPaths=["../outside.txt"], run dispatch_run, then inspect .koala/dispatches/<dispatchId>/prompt.md; it contains "Only edit these paths: ../outside.txt" while the worktree is .worktrees/overflow/<story>/<dispatch>.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit b7b16fcf. Dispatch pack allowedPaths/deniedPaths are now normalized before prompt metadata is persisted, and real-host scaffold revalidates paths against the actual worktree before returning needs_receipt. Smoke now covers real-host traversal rejection before metadata persists and real-host symlink escape rejection before needs_receipt. Verified with build, dispatch-run smoke, lattice-handoff smoke, host-overflow smoke, command ownership contract, process fact contract, git diff --check, and lattice validate test command output.

findings.desc: dispatchId path traversal escapes .koala/dispatches and allows out-of-scope Lattice metadata writes. dispatchDir/dispatchFile join caller-controlled dispatchId into storage paths, and prepareDispatch accepts args.dispatchId from the public handler unchanged. Repro: dispatch_prepare --dispatchId=../../../outside/owned writes dispatch.json, pack.json, prompt.md, and transcript.log outside the repository dispatch storage root. Apply validation to all public dispatchId read/write paths and add smoke coverage for malicious dispatchId.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit b7b16fcf. dispatchId is now validated at the storage helper/read-write boundary and rejected for empty, absolute, separator, or traversal values across prepare/run/status/collect/receipt/resume/cancel/review/merge_plan. Smoke now covers malicious dispatchId rejection across those commands and proves no metadata is written outside .koala/dispatches. Verified with build, dispatch-run smoke, lattice-handoff smoke, host-overflow smoke, command ownership contract, process fact contract, git diff --check, and lattice validate test command output.

findings.desc: README dispatch examples use --allowedPath, but the landed CLI only honors --allowedPaths. dispatch_plan with --allowedPath leaves pack.allowedPaths empty, while --allowedPaths populates it. Update README examples to match the actual dispatch CLI schema.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 5856f39b. README dispatch examples now use the landed CLI parameter --allowedPaths instead of the non-existent --allowedPath. Verified by docs grep and build/dispatch-run smoke plus full validation command output.

findings.desc: dispatchId hardening coverage is missing the overflow_auto public entrypoint. The malicious-id smoke matrix covers dispatch_prepare/run/status/collect/receipt/resume/cancel/review/merge_plan but not overflow_auto, even though overflow_auto accepts dispatchId and has both suggest-only and approve+start paths. Add smoke assertions for overflow_auto --dispatchId=../../dispatch-id-escape in suggest-only no-write mode and approve+start rejection/no outside metadata write.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 5856f39b. dispatch-run smoke now covers overflow_auto with a malicious dispatchId in suggest-only mode as a no-write path and in approve+start mode as a rejected path, proving no outside .koala/dispatches metadata write. Verified with build and npm --prefix packages/main run test:dispatch-run-smoke plus related smoke/contract commands.

findings.desc: Real-host dispatch_run creates the overflow worktree before symlink-aware canonical pack-path validation completes. Repro: prepare a codex dispatch with allowedPaths=["packages/main/src/generated/external-link/blocked-by-symlink.txt"] and run dispatch_run. It throws the symlink escape error, but the projected worktree exists afterward and dispatch.json remains status=prepared. The smoke only asserts the throw and no external write, not cleanup/failed state. This violates the boundary that real-host scaffold should happen only after bounded pack paths.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 5856f39b. Real-host post-scaffold canonical pack-path validation failure now becomes a structured failed dispatch result: it appends transcript evidence, cleans up the worktree when created by this run, persists status=failed, returns authorityChanged=false/receiptVerified=false/productionDone=false, and gives a corrective nextAction instead of throwing while leaving prepared residue. Smoke asserts failed status, no external write, worktree cleanup, and persisted failed state.

findings.desc: Preexisting symlinked projected worktree root bypasses dispatch containment. ensureWorktree reuses any existing .worktrees/overflow/... path without validating that it is a real registered git worktree. If that path is a symlink to an external directory, fake dispatch can write outside the repo before git fails, and real-host dispatch can return needs_receipt for an external target. Reject symlink/non-worktree roots before reuse and add fake plus real-host root-symlink smoke coverage.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by existing HEAD 241b9000. ensureWorktree now rejects existing projected overflow worktree roots unless they are non-symlink directories, resolve inside the repository, match git rev-parse --show-toplevel, and are registered in git worktree list before fake writes or real-host needs_receipt. dispatch-run smoke covers fake and real preexisting root-symlink cases. Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build and npm --prefix packages/main run test:dispatch-run-smoke.

findings.desc: Ancestor symlink in .worktrees/overflow can still materialize an out-of-repo worktree before containment rejects it. If .worktrees/overflow/<storyId> is a symlink to an external directory, ensureWorktree calls git worktree add through that symlink and only afterward assertRegisteredDispatchWorktreeRoot rejects the external realpath. This leaves external worktree artifacts for fake and real-host dispatches even though they do not reach needs_receipt. Validate all existing worktreePath ancestors before mkdirSync/git worktree add, clean partial add failures, and add fake plus real-host ancestor-symlink smoke coverage.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by committed code in 7beea13d with validation preserved by 87480a9c. Dispatch worktree creation now validates projected ancestors before mkdir/git worktree add, and dispatch-run smoke covers fake plus real-host .worktrees/overflow/<storyId> ancestor symlink attacks with no external artifacts. Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build; npm --prefix packages/main run test:dispatch-run-smoke; npm --prefix packages/main run test:capability-list-smoke.

findings.desc: Gemini dispatch artifacts collapse into Codex semantics instead of preserving host-neutral identity. dispatch_prepare with host=gemini persists pack.toHost=codex and prompt instructions that say to use codex, because handoffTargetForRuntime maps every non-claude runtime to codex and capability profiles do not include Gemini. B-106b cannot certify host-neutral overflow across supported hosts until Gemini dispatches use a Gemini/host-neutral target identity and smoke coverage verifies pack/prompt artifacts for Gemini.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by implementer commit 7beea13d. Gemini is now a first-class capability profile, handoffTargetForRuntime preserves host=gemini as toHost=gemini, and dispatch-run smoke asserts Gemini dispatch pack/prompt artifacts say Gemini and do not silently fall back to Codex wording. Verified with build, dispatch-run smoke, capability-list smoke, handoff/host-overflow smokes, command/process contracts, and git diff --check.

findings.desc: Mixed parallel fake-worker outcomes collapse to failed instead of the contract-required recoverable diagnostic/partial parent outcome. CHK-015 says one worker failure yields diagnostic/partial while preserving successful worker receipts, but aggregateStatus returns failed when any worker failed and smoke only covers all-workers-success plus separate single-leaf failure.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 87480a9c. aggregateStatus now returns diagnostic for mixed terminal worker outcomes while preserving uniform all-success, all-failed, all-cancelled, all-expired, and all-unavailable outcomes; dispatch-run smoke covers one accepted_local fake worker plus one failed worker, preserves the successful receipt, reports parent diagnostic, makes dispatch_review non-accepted, and keeps dispatch_merge_plan non-mergeable. Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build; npm --prefix packages/main run test:dispatch-run-smoke; npm --prefix packages/main run test:capability-list-smoke.

findings.desc: Cross-host receipt artifacts are still codex-pinned. createFakeReceipt and dispatch_receipt_create hardcode host="codex" in receipt payloads (packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:995 and :1497), while the handoff receipt schema treats host as the receipt producer host beside fromHost/toHost (packages/main/src/core/lattice-handoff.ts:181-204). dispatch-run-smoke only verifies Gemini host identity in pack/prompt artifacts (packages/main/src/tasks/dispatch-run-smoke.ts:365-389) and misses receipt artifacts. Repro: prepare a gemini dispatch and run dispatch_receipt_create; the emitted receipt reports {"host":"codex","toHost":"gemini"}. This violates the host-neutral Gemini/Codex artifact boundary.
